Escape in a Car.
Mahmud Rashid, aged 33, a railway turner, declared in his confession that he was a member of the so-called "Society of Vengeance." He asserted that Hamid Enaiat, another accused, spoke to him as regards, murdering the Sirdar. Mahmud Rashid lent his motor-car, and they went to the scene of the outrage and waited in the car until the outrage had been accomplished, when they escaped with Hamid Enaiat and Ibrahim Musa.

label: text

label: text
text: Shafik Mansour, in his confession, declared that Mahmud Ismail told him that Great Britain must understand that there was always in Egypt a force decided to end British acts of violence by individual reprisals. Shafik Mansour said he did not agree with the crime against the Sirdat, because he believed it would cause harm to Egypt, and the two Enaiats promised to abstain from the attempt, but while he was at the Ministry of Education, he heard of the outrage, and on returning to his house he saw Hamid Enaiat, who informed him of the crime, whereupon he approached Hamid Enaiat for having committed the outrage.

label: paragraph_title
text: Secret Society.

label: text
text: Mohamed Fahmy, who admitted having committed 'outrages against various Europeans,' but disclaimed participation in 'the murder of the Sirdar, in referring to other political outrages confessed to the existence of a secret society for the organisation of crimes, of which he, the two Enaiats, Ibrahim Musa, Mahmud Rashid, Shafik Mansour, and Mahmud Ismail were all members.' He declared that Shatik Mansour, whose confession is given above, was involved in all the political crimes.

label: text
text: The Sirdar of Egypt, Sir Lee Oliver Stack, G.B.E., C.M.G., was fatally injured on November 19. Two bornbs were thrown at him as he was driving from the Ministry of War. Three of the four assailants escaped when the one bomb did not explode. They fired several rounds from revolvers, hitting Sir Lee Stack, his Aide-de-Camp; Captain Campbell of the Black Watch, the chauffeur and a policeman. The Sirdar was badly wounded in the stomach and had to be taken to hospital, where he later succumbed. The attack on the Sirdar was made in Shariakas Relaini, a main and busy thoroughfare of Cairo. The chauffeur, despite his wounds, drove off at full speed and brought the car to the Residency, which is nearer than the Sirdaria. (Sirdar's residence).

label: text

label: paragraph_title
text: SUDDEN RISING

label: text
text: The Spanish Embassy in London discredits the story of an attempt on the Spanish Royal Train and says the report is merely a part of a campaign to discredit Spain.

label: text
text: [Travellers from Barcelona have persistently reported an attempt to blow up the train in which the King and Queen of Spain had arranged to go to Madrid. A bomb weighing eighty kilograms was said to have been found in a tunnel, and nineteen arrests were reported to have been made. Their Majesties were said to have postponed their departure and to be remaining at Barcelona.]

label: text
text: Berlin, June 6.—Authoritative political circles are of opinion that the Allied Powers display complete misconception of the extent of Germany's disarmament. It is stated that the conception that Germany has formed an army in proportion to her population is entirely opposed to facts. Nevertheless the Government is prepared immediately to carefully examine and note the remedy for any failures to carry out her obligations. It is emphasised, however, that Germany cannot go beyond the loyal interpretation of the Treaty of Versailles and the Government's one aim is lasting peace.—Reuter.

text: Trouble has broken out on the island of Samos where insurgents have seized government buildings, arrested officials, released prisoners

label: text
text: Whether the movement is political or more net of banditry on the part of two notorious influential Summan brignnds, the brothers Vafiades, is not yet clear, but it is known the leaders are demanding the resignation of the Greek Government and fresh elections, though this may be more cannotflage.

label: paragraph_title
text: COTTON NEEDS.

label: paragraph_title
text:
VIENNA CONGRESS
VIEWS.

label: paragraph_title
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: VIENNA, June 7.

label: text
text: The international "cotton congress has passed a resolution expressing the opinion that the world's statistical position in cotton is such as to warrant an extension of cotton growing wherever feasible on commercial bases; urging the governments of all countries where cotton can be produced advantageously to stimulate development of cotton growing by increasing the cultivated area; creating efficient transport; recogning the construction of irrigation and drainage works such as are being undertaken in the Sudan and India which are the proper means of bringing about an increased supply of cotton; and fervently hoping that all governments will decide on similar works where it is shown the cotton crop will be considerably increased by means of irrigation.

label: text
text: At the final sitting of the cotton conference the chairman, M. Buhler, of Switzerland, referred to irrigation proceeding in India and Sudan and declared that was the best way the Governments could extend cotton growing. He added that the high price of the American product, which was likely to continue, was injuring the welfare of the industry.

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: (Keuter's Service.)

label: text
text: KINGSTON, JAMAICA, June 7. The Governor, Sir Samuel Wilson, is going to England on June 8 for two months leave of absence on medical grounds.

label: text
text: He will discuss with the Secretary of Colonies, Mr. L. M. S. Amery, among other matters, alien immigration which was discussed by the legislature recently, when it was declared Jamaica would be ruined unless steps were taken to prevent further immigration of Chinese and Syrians.

label: paragraph_title

label: text

label: text
text: RIGA, June 7.

label: text
text: A large party of Russian emigrants who were converted to Bolshevism while in the United States have arrived at Libau en route to Russia bringing tractors and other agricultural machinery with a view to reconstructing the agricultural life of the country.

label: text
text: Paris, June 6.—A "Temps" correspondent in Morocco learns that the Spanish will begin operations in ten days' time against Abd El Krim's capital, Adjur. An expeditionary force is landing in the neighbourhood of Albucernis, covered by the fleet and airforce. It is stated that General De Riveri will personally direct operations from aboard a cruiser.—Reuter.

label: text
text: King Victor Emmanuel III. is 55 years of age. He succeeded to the throne in 1900, on the assassination of his father, King Humbert. He married in 1896 Princess Helene of Montenegro.

label: text
text: King Victor took a prominent part in the relief of victims at Messina after the 1908 earthquake.

label: text
text: He is industrious, amiable, and well read.

label: text
text: He led his nation to join the cause of the Allies in the spring of 1915 amid great enthusiasm. His eldest daughter, Princess Yolanda, married Count Calvi di Bergolo, on April 9, 1923.
